# Are the Son and the Spirit God, and three persons?


When Thomas saw the risen Jesus he answered him, "My Lord and my God!" (John
20:28). John's Gospel opens with the same claim: "In the beginning was the Word,
and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (John 1:1). Peter tells Ananias,
who had lied "to the Holy Spirit", that he had "not lied to man but to God" (Acts
5:3–4). Ken Kibbey's *Living Systematic Theology* (LST) gathers these texts with
others and confesses: "The Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is
God; they are personally distinct without being separate gods."

That sentence makes two claims, and each has a rival that reads the same verses
otherwise. The first is that the Son and the Spirit are God. Jehovah's Witnesses
deny it. The second is that Father, Son and Spirit are three persons, none of
them the other. Oneness Pentecostals deny that, and they agree with LST against
the Witnesses on the first. So the question divides three ways, and the texts
each side cites are mostly the same texts.

## Three readings of the same verses

The Witnesses' brochure *Should You Believe in the Trinity?* (1989) reads John
1:1 from the Greek. The first "God" in "the Word was with God" has the article,
"the" (τὸν θεόν); the second, in "the Word was God", has none (θεός). "So John
1:1 highlights the quality of the Word, that he was 'divine,' 'godlike,' 'a god,'
but not Almighty God" (p. 27). Their New World Translation renders the clause
"and the Word was a god". Colossians 1:15 calls the Son "the firstborn of all
creation", and the brochure reads it as "Jesus was created by God as the beginning
of God's invisible creations" (p. 14). Of Thomas it offers two readings: "To
Thomas, Jesus was like 'a god'", or the words were an exclamation "spoken to Jesus
but directed to God"; "in either case, Thomas did not think that Jesus was
Almighty God" (p. 29). On "with God" the brochure is on LST's side against the
Oneness reading: "Someone who is 'with' another person cannot be the same as that
other person" (p. 27). The holy spirit is
"God's active force that he uses to accomplish his will", and "personifying the
holy spirit" does not "make it a spirit person" (pp. 21, 23).

Philip Harner's study of the same grammar (1973) reads the clause the other way.
A noun without the article placed before the verb, as θεός is here, is
"primarily qualitative": it says what kind of thing the Word is. "They indicate
that the logos has the nature of theos" (as the New World Translation's reference
edition quotes him). Augustine answers the Arians from John 1:3: "How can it be
that the Word of God was made, when God by the Word made all things? … that by
which all things were made could not be made by itself" (*Tractates on John*
I.11). Calvin reads Acts 5:4 as Peter saying that "he lieth to God who doth lie to
the Holy Ghost. For the divinity of the Holy Ghost is manifestly proved by this
form of speech."

David Bernard's *The Oneness of God* (1983) grants all of that. "Jesus is the one
God" (ch. 4), and the Holy Spirit is God, as "a comparison of Acts 5:3 with 5:4"
shows (ch. 6). What he denies is that "with God" means a second person. "The Word
was not a separate person or a separate god any more than a man's word is a
separate person from him. Rather the Word was the thought, plan, or mind of God"
(ch. 4). When Jesus prays for "the glory that I had with you before the world
existed" (John 17:5), he speaks of "the glory the Son had in the plan of God from
the beginning" (ch. 8). And the "name" of Matthew 28:19 is one name, not three:
"the one name of Matthew 28:19 is Jesus" (ch. 6).

## What is checked

Each verse is a claim of its own, and each reading of it is another, cited to the
reader who holds it and rated `disputed`, the lowest rating, because the other
readers deny it. LST's case has three lines. From John 1:1, 1:3 and 20:28, with
Harner's and Augustine's readings, the Word is God (`wordLine`). From Acts 5:3–4,
with Calvin's reading, the Spirit is God (`spiritLine`). From "with God", the
glory before the world, the Spirit who says "set apart for me" (Acts 13:2), and
the three named in Matthew 28:19, each read as LST reads it, there are three
persons (`personsLine`). Together with the one God of Deuteronomy 6:4, they give
LST's confession (`lstDeity_establishes`). The Witnesses' case gives the Son a
creature and not God (`witnesses_establish`). The Oneness case holds LST's first
two lines and adds its own readings of the "with" texts, and gives one person,
not three (`oneness_establishes`). Each position can be held without
contradiction.

These results say what follows from each set of readings. They do not say which
readings are right, and they do not say that the bare texts, without any reading,
settle the question either way. The next chapter weighs the three positions
against one another.

## What is not heard

Many texts on each side are left out. For the Witnesses: John 14:28, which the
chapter on the order hears; John 17:3, "you, the only true God", which the
brochure cites against Thomas's words; and John 10:34, where Jesus quotes "you
are gods" (Psalm 82:6), from which the brochure argues that the Son "can be and
is 'a god'" (p. 28). For LST: Hebrews 1:8, Titus 2:13, Romans 9:5, and the texts
that apply to Jesus what the Old Testament says of the LORD, Isaiah 45:23 in
Philippians 2:10–11 among them. John 20:28 enters as a text that every party
grants, with no reading of its own: neither of the brochure's two readings of
Thomas's words is a premise here, so what divides the parties over the Son is
carried by their readings of John 1:1, 1:3 and Colossians 1:15. What is found here
is what these verses and these readings carry, and no more.

- (4) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-38}{P_{38}}\\) — Acts 13:2; Ephesians 4:30 — the Spirit says "set apart for me", and is grieved
- (5) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-50}{P_{50}}\\) — The holy spirit is God's active force, personified, not a person
- (6) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-34}{P_{34}}\\) — John 1:1 — "and the Word was God", θεός without the article
- (7) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-36}{P_{36}}\\) — John 20:28 — "Thomas answered him, 'My Lord and my God!'"
- (8) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-37}{P_{37}}\\) — Acts 5:3–4 — "lie to the Holy Spirit … not to man but to God"
- (9) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}}\\) — John 1:1 — "the Word was with God"
- (10) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-46}{P_{46}}\\) — "With God" (John 1:1; 17:5) is one person beside another, not a thought or plan
- (11) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-34}{P_{34}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-41}{P_{41}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-48}{P_{48}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-49}{P_{49}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-57}{P_{57}}\\) — *would give:* The Son is a creature, the first of God's works, and not God
- (12) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-38}{P_{38}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-50}{P_{50}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-45}{P_{45}}\\) — *would deny:* The Spirit who speaks and is grieved is a person, not a force
- (13) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-57}{P_{57}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\)
- (14) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-50}{P_{50}} \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-55}{P_{55}}\\) — *would deny:* The Holy Spirit is God
- \\(\vdash\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\) — *at issue, the denial of:* The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created

</div>

Grounded in scripture alone: Colossians 1:15 — "the firstborn of all creation", Acts 13:2; Ephesians 4:30 — the Spirit says "set apart for me", and is grieved, John 1:1 — "and the Word was God", θεός without the article, John 20:28 — "Thomas answered him, 'My Lord and my God!'", Acts 5:3–4 — "lie to the Holy Spirit … not to man but to God", John 1:1 — "the Word was with God".

### Oneness: one God, one person

<a id="onePersonUnderThreeTitles"></a>
**`onePersonUnderThreeTitles`**

The Oneness step: the Word God's thought, the glory in his plan, and the one
name Jesus, so not three persons.

<div class="testimony-derivation">

- \\((\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\) — *would deny:* The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three persons

</div>

<a id="onenessLine"></a>
**`onenessLine`** — God's Word, God's plan, and the one name (Oneness)

**The Oneness line.**

<div class="testimony-derivation">

- (1) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}}\\) — John 1:1 — "the Word was with God"
- (2) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}}\\) — John 17:5 — "the glory that I had with you before the world existed"
- (3) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}}\\) — Matthew 28:19 — "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit"
- (4) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}}\\) — The Word of John 1:1 is God's thought and self-expression, not a second person
- (5) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}}\\) — The glory of John 17:5 was the Son's in God's plan before the world
- (6) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}\\) — The one "name" of Matthew 28:19 is Jesus; Father, Son and Spirit are titles
- (7) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\)
- \\(\vdash\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\) — *at issue, the denial of:* The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three persons

</div>

<a id="onenessCase"></a>
**`onenessCase`** — One God, one person (Oneness)

**The Oneness position**: the Word is God and the Spirit is God, as LST
holds, and they are one person with the Father, not three.

<div class="testimony-derivation">

- (1) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-32}{P_{32}}\\) — Deuteronomy 6:4; 1 Corinthians 8:4 — "the LORD is one"; "no God but one"
- (2) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-34}{P_{34}}\\) — John 1:1 — "and the Word was God", θεός without the article
- (3) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-35}{P_{35}}\\) — John 1:3 — "all things were made through him"
- (4) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-36}{P_{36}}\\) — John 20:28 — "Thomas answered him, 'My Lord and my God!'"
- (5) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-42}{P_{42}}\\) — In John 1:1c θεός says the Word has the nature of the one God
- (6) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-43}{P_{43}}\\) — By John 1:3 the Word is not among the things made
- (7) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-37}{P_{37}}\\) — Acts 5:3–4 — "lie to the Holy Spirit … not to man but to God"
- (8) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-44}{P_{44}}\\) — In Acts 5:3–4 Peter names the Holy Spirit God
- (9) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}}\\) — John 1:1 — "the Word was with God"
- (10) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}}\\) — John 17:5 — "the glory that I had with you before the world existed"
- (11) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}}\\) — Matthew 28:19 — "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit"
- (12) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}}\\) — The Word of John 1:1 is God's thought and self-expression, not a second person
- (13) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}}\\) — The glory of John 17:5 was the Son's in God's plan before the world
- (14) \\(\href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}\\) — The one "name" of Matthew 28:19 is Jesus; Father, Son and Spirit are titles
- (15) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-32}{P_{32}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-34}{P_{34}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-35}{P_{35}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-36}{P_{36}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-42}{P_{42}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-43}{P_{43}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-54}{P_{54}}\\) — *would give:* The Word who became flesh in Jesus is God, of God's nature and not created
- (16) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-37}{P_{37}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-44}{P_{44}}) \rightarrow \href{claims.html#claim-55}{P_{55}}\\) — *would give:* The Holy Spirit is God
- (17) \\((\href{claims.html#claim-33}{P_{33}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-39}{P_{39}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-40}{P_{40}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-51}{P_{51}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-52}{P_{52}} \land \href{claims.html#claim-53}{P_{53}}) \rightarrow \lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\)
- \\(\vdash\\) \\(\lnot \href{claims.html#claim-56}{P_{56}}\\) — *at issue, the denial of:* The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three persons

</div>

Grounded in scripture alone: Deuteronomy 6:4; 1 Corinthians 8:4 — "the LORD is one"; "no God but one", John 1:1 — "and the Word was God", θεός without the article, John 1:3 — "all things were made through him", John 20:28 — "Thomas answered him, 'My Lord and my God!'", Acts 5:3–4 — "lie to the Holy Spirit … not to man but to God", John 1:1 — "the Word was with God", John 17:5 — "the glory that I had with you before the world existed", Matthew 28:19 — "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit".

### Readings, written down

<a id="nicenReading"></a>
**`nicenReading`**

**The Nicene reading**: every text, every Nicene reading, and the
confession; none of the Witnesses' readings or the Oneness ones.

```lean
def nicenReading : Valuation Claim :=
  fun a =>
    match a with
    | Claim.wordIsAGod => False
    | Claim.firstbornIsFirstCreated => False
    | Claim.spiritIsGodsForce => False
    | Claim.sonIsACreature => False
    | Claim.wordIsGodsThought => False
    | Claim.gloryInGodsPlan => False
    | Claim.oneNameIsJesus => False
    | x => True
```

<a id="witnessesReading"></a>
**`witnessesReading`**

**The Witnesses' reading**: every text, "a god", the firstborn first created,
the spirit a force; the Son a creature and not God, the spirit neither a person
nor God. None of the Nicene readings, none of the Oneness ones, and not three
persons.

```lean
def witnessesReading : Valuation Claim :=
  fun a =>
    match a with
    | Claim.wordIsGodByNature => False
    | Claim.wordIsUnmade => False
    | Claim.spiritLiedToIsGod => False
    | Claim.spiritIsAPerson => False
    | Claim.threeNamedInOneName => False
    | Claim.wordIsGodsThought => False
    | Claim.gloryInGodsPlan => False
    | Claim.oneNameIsJesus => False
    | Claim.wordIsGod => False
    | Claim.spiritIsGod => False
    | Claim.threePersons => False
    | Claim.triuneGod => False
    | x => True
```

<a id="onenessReading"></a>
**`onenessReading`**

**The Oneness reading**: every text, the Nicene readings of John 1:1c, 1:3
and Acts 5, the Word and the Spirit God; the Oneness readings, and not three
persons.

```lean
def onenessReading : Valuation Claim :=
  fun a =>
    match a with
    | Claim.wordIsAGod => False
    | Claim.firstbornIsFirstCreated => False
    | Claim.spiritIsGodsForce => False
    | Claim.sonIsACreature => False
    | Claim.wordIsAnotherWithGod => False
    | Claim.threeNamedInOneName => False
    | Claim.threePersons => False
    | Claim.triuneGod => False
    | x => True
```

### What each position delivers

<a id="lstDeity_establishes"></a>
**`lstDeity_establishes`**

**Grant the Nicene readings of John 1:1 and 1:3, of Acts 5:3–4, and of the
texts that name three, and LST's confession follows**: the Father, the Son and
the Spirit are God, three persons and one God.

```lean
theorem lstDeity_establishes : Establishes lstDeityCase
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="lstDeityCase_is_satisfiable"></a>
**`lstDeityCase_is_satisfiable`**

LST's position can be held without contradiction.

```lean
theorem lstDeityCase_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable lstDeityCase.premises
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="witnesses_establish"></a>
**`witnesses_establish`**

**Grant John 1:1c read as "a god" and Colossians 1:15 as the first thing
made, and the Son is a creature, not God.**

```lean
theorem witnesses_establish : Establishes witnessesCase
-- axioms: propext, Quot.sound
```

<a id="witnessesCase_is_satisfiable"></a>

The Witnesses' position can be held without contradiction.

```lean
theorem witnessesCase_is_satisfiable : Satisfiable witnessesCase.premises

```
